description: A 32 by 32 grid of coloured lamps that paints itself one pixel at a time, reading the red, green and blue jacks at each pixel in turn and reporting the position it has reached on the X and Y outputs

params.text: Sets the range of the X output: unipolar runs 0V to 10V across the width of the grid, bipolar runs -5V to 5V
Sets the range of the Y output: unipolar runs 0V to 10V down the height of the grid, bipolar runs -5V to 5V
Sets how many samples the scan spends on each pixel before moving on, 1 to 30, so a whole frame takes that many samples times 1024 pixels
Scales the red input before the red offset is added, -1 to 1; at 1 a 10V signal gives full red
Sets the red of every pixel on its own while nothing is patched to the red jack, and is added to that jack when something is; 0 for none and 1 for full
Scales the green input before the green offset is added, -1 to 1; at 1 a 10V signal gives full green
Sets the green of every pixel on its own while nothing is patched to the green jack, and is added to that jack when something is; 0 for none and 1 for full
Scales the blue input before the blue offset is added, -1 to 1; at 1 a 10V signal gives full blue
Sets the blue of every pixel on its own while nothing is patched to the blue jack, and is added to that jack when something is; 0 for none and 1 for full
Starts a new frame while a cable is patched to the trigger jack; with that jack empty a new frame begins on its own as soon as the last one ends and this button changes nothing

inputs.text: Sets the red of the pixel the scan has reached, through the red scale and offset knobs
Sets the green of the pixel the scan has reached, through the green scale and offset knobs
Sets the blue of the pixel the scan has reached, through the blue scale and offset knobs
Starts a new frame on each rising edge above 1V; with this jack empty a new frame begins on its own as soon as the last one ends

outputs.text: The horizontal position of the pixel being painted, a staircase of 32 steps across the width of the grid
A square wave that rises for the first half of the samples spent on each pixel and falls for the second half; with the sample knob at 1 it alternates from one pixel to the next instead
The vertical position of the pixel being painted, a staircase of 32 steps down the height of the grid
10V while the scan is in the left half of a row and 0V while it is in the right half, which gives one cycle per row
10V while the scan is on the last pixel of a frame and 0V for the rest of the frame

notes: the grid stays black until something is patched to the red, green or blue jacks or one of the offset knobs is turned up; the scan itself runs whether or not anything is patched
the lamp is red while no frame is being painted, flashes green as each frame starts, and carries blue while polyphonic mode is on
menu: Polyphonic mode — paints sixteen pixels at once, taking one from each channel of the red, green and blue jacks, and gives the X and Y outputs sixteen channels
Double-buffered — holds a new frame back until it is complete, so the grid changes all at once instead of being painted across
Fade lights — lets each lamp slide towards its new colour instead of jumping to it

inputs.0:
0 to 10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the red offset knob.
inputs.1:
0 to 10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the green offset knob.
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the blue offset knob.
inputs.3:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads a frame starts by itself; a negative voltage does nothing here.
